utterances.text: I hate to interrupt this argument, but is counsel conceding that Simo Zaric did in fact interrogate his wife?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simo Zaric never had any conversation with Mrs. Esma Fitozovic, the wife of the witness, Alija Fitozovic. That is what he claims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Maybe this is just a question of semantics here, but you've just said: "Mr. Simo Zaric never had any conversation with," and previously you've said that he had a conversation with the wife re: The fleeing of the husband. So I think we need more precise language. You've admitted or you've stated he did have a conversation. Maybe you need to refine the language to make the point clear for the record that you're putting to us, "conversation" versus "interrogation" or something similar, conversation in the street conversation or interrogation in an official building, office. I think we this clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that I was very precise. I'm not listening to the interpretation, and I don't know what was said there. I said that at one time he saw her at the police station, and then I said that Mr. Zaric never officially interrogated or officially interviewed or talked with Mrs. Esma Fitozovic, the wife of Alija Fitozovic. That's what I said. So he did not interrogate or talk to her in any official capacity that had to do with gathering of any kind of official information. I did say that he saw her and that Esma at that time was angry, and she said why she was angry with Mr. Alija Fitozovic, that it was because she left and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your wife ever say to you that Simo Zaric had any kind of an interview with her or took a statement from her in the police station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Zaric interrogated my wife. Her name is Esma Fitozovic. And he was -- he showed her the same documents that you showed me today, and he asked her whether the handwriting was mine. My wife, at that time, told her [As interpreted] that we live in modern times and that she talks to me on the phone when needed, and that she does not write -- that we do not have a letter correspondence. That was my wife's answer to Simo Zaric at the police station in Samac. There is no doubt about that, and you said yourself a little bit earlier that he interrogated her once, and then you said that he talked to her, and a third time, that she was angry with me because I left, as if I was supposed to stay in the atmosphere of well-being that the 4th Detachment imposed on the citizens of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, sir. You heard all of this from your wife, Mr. Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and now from you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I only have one further question. You saw a document yesterday, D21/1. This was the list of traitors; is that correct? And you said about that list that you were the author of it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I take another look at this document? I do not remember it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the number of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document D21/1 and D21/1 ter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get the document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you said yesterday that you were the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I said that yesterday, I am certainly standing by it today. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read the first list --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first name on the list of local traitors. Who is the first person?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadil Topcagic, nicknamed Brada.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read what else is written here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Chetnik duke, or Vojvoda."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Topcagic, Fadil is the brother of Simo Zaric's wife; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now please read the fifth name.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Denis Topcagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read what you said about him.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The butcher's aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that Denis Topcagic is the son of Simo Zaric's wife, Fatima?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction. He is the son of Simo Zaric's wife's brother.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now please read the name under number 7.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dedic Huso and son.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have some misunderstanding here in the transcript. I'm sorry for interrupting. He's the son of Simo Zaric's wife's brother. That's not true. The question was: Is he a son of Simo Zaric's wife. Maybe for clarification it is from her first marriage, so maybe this confused the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pisarevic can correct that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Fitozovic, can you confirm that Denis Topcagic is the son of Fatima Zaric, from her earlier life?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Topcagic Denis is Fatima's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she is Simo Zaric's wife?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she is Simo Zaric's wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the seventh name, can you read it out, please?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Huso Dedic and son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please also read what you said about them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hand grenade launchers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Dedic, Huso and his son Senad are closely related with Ms. Fatima?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, this is the first time I hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need that document any more. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, you said that you had only one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just conclude. Let me just conclude this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said more than once --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one. This is the last one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said more than once in your testimony, you mentioned Fadil Topcagic more than once in your testimony, and the relatives of Simo Zaric's wife, that is to say, Fatima Zaric's relatives. Can you confirm the fact that your relationship, that is to say, your relationship with the family of Fatima Zaric, in 1991 and 1992, was very strained? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a good relationship with them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. You mean 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, in April -- well, not in April of 1992, so not in 1992. But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, can you let the witness complete his answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then I would have to say two things: Until the first half of 1991, our relationship was good. Then in September of 1991, I was with Mr. Simo Zaric --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not talk about Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Until 1991, the relationship was good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second half of 1991, until 1992, the relationship was not so good, but there was no hatred either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am done with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask if we're going to have a break in this hour and a half that I intend to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because of our earlier break, the next break is at 1650.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Fitozovic. My name is Novak Lukic. I'm attorney at law and I represent Mr. Miroslav Tadic. I'm going to start my cross-examination. And with regard to the time that I said I would allocate to this cross-examination, I would like to ask you to be very quick so that we can end this part as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first couple of questions will have to do with the topic that you -- that was already mentioned yesterday. I actually only have one question about this. When you answered Mr. Pisarevic, and also the Prosecutor, when you talked to them about the truck that broke down in Samac, and when you talked about this deal that two crates of the weapons should be given to you as payment for the transfer of weapons into another truck - you remember, this right? - my question is very simple: Did the driver of this truck tell you where the transfer was headed? Who was it for?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said he was going in the direction of Central Bosnia or Sarajevo. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say for what individual institution or organisation the weapons were for?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday and the day before you also said that up until September of 1991 you were a member of the HDZ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us now up until what time you were an active member of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an active member of the HDZ while I was active in the organisation. I don't know. Maybe two or three months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I remember we did go through this quite a lot with Mr. Pisarevic. I think if you check the transcript, you'll find the answers there. And this is what I was trying to say yesterday, that I don't want repetition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. My questions will not be repetitions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about a meeting that took place in Odzak in August of 1991? This meeting was a meeting of the leaders of the HDZ party and they were talking about establishing the region of Bosanski Posavina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have no further questions on this topic. On the 27th of May, while testifying to the Prosecutor, you said the following, and I'm going to read this out because it's been a couple of days since then. When you answered the question about the atmosphere in the town, you said the following. [In English] "There were people from abroad who were not from the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Some people in uniforms were passing through." [Interpretation] Do you remember stating this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to talk just about the period up to the 17th of April. You said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have no objection to counsel referring to the transcript. Could he just cite the page so we can follow along, especially if there's going to be a lot of discussion about, you know, previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. If you can indicate the pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read this on page 60, line 8 and 9 of the unofficial transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that people wearing uniforms were seen in the town. Did you personally see people in uniforms in the town?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of uniforms were these, these uniforms that you personally saw?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's clarify. These were JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the so-called JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see members of the ZNG, that is to say, the Croatian National Guard Corps, in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally go to a discotheque at Cuse's [phoen]? Do you know this establishment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to this discotheque, this cafe?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there, but not very frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your informers, that is to say, patrol members, or did somebody else tell you that these members of the Croatian National Guard Corps frequently patronised this discotheque in uniform in the winter?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell me anything about this. I have no idea about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP, on the 2nd of December, 1991, dispatched a group of its specials, 30 members of its special units, to patrol and to join the police station in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but they were not sent there for this purpose. So can I say no. My answer to your question will be no, because they were not sent there to patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can say quite clearly and freely as to your knowledge about the purpose why they were sent there.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will do so when you ask me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. According to your knowledge, why did the specials from Sarajevo come to Bosanski Samac, I mean the members of the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to Bosanski Samac because in December, in fact, in November or December, a sabotage had been carried out on the bridge across the Sava River, connecting the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia. That was their main task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether their arrival has anything to do with the demobilisation of the police force in the Bosanski Samac police station?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was demobilised at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will move on to another topic. Mr. Fitozovic, did you ever set foot in the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough idea, or perhaps even a precise idea, as to when it was that you went into that cafe for the last time before the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been in November 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that the picture of President Tito was there in the cafe when you were there last?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber feels that maybe we'll give a break, because the witness appears exhausted. We'll go earlier than I thought we should. We can have another break for 20 minutes, I think, and resume our proceedings at 1700 hours. We shall have another 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has been informed that the witness is extremely upset and unable to continue today. So I wanted to find out from the Prosecution what their plans are. Is he going it come on Monday or another day?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the way things were going, it looked like Attorney Lukac had at least another hour to hour and a half of cross-examination, so it would have gone into Monday any way. Then attorney Pantelic was going to cross-examine and then myself on re-direct. Either way we're going on Monday so I don't think it makes much of a difference. We'll just continue on with him and finish -- do as we were going to do, finish him off on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we continue with him on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And after him then we have Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. We have a witness who is in transit right now, will be here probably late today, and we would do that probably Monday, Tuesday, and then followed by probably Mr. Todorovic. MR. DI FAZIO: May I address you on that issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because the Trial Chamber is mindful of the fact that Mr. Todorovic has a limited period. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I appreciate that, if Your Honours please. He's coming this weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm told, I'm informed by those who are making arrangements for him to be brought here. I tried to make arrangements to get access to him this weekend for the purpose of proofing him. I've mentioned to you in the past that I do need to proof him, finish proofing him. Proofing him has taken a long time. I've gone to a country where he's currently imprisoned to proof him, and that process is still incomplete. When I was speaking to Registry officials making arrangements, speaking to them about arrangements for him to be brought here, I was informed by in fact Mr. Christian Rohde that the difficulty that the faced was not the period of time that he spent here but rather them having sufficient notice for them to make arrangements for him to be brought here, and so I made the -- put in the appropriate motion and so on. And of course he's coming here and that probably is now gone. However, I was given to understand by Mr. Rohde that keeping him here is not a matter that's of great concern or going to cause any sort of fundamental problem. Secondly, I note from the order or decision, the confidential decision of the Chamber regarding his testimony that the Chamber takes the view that the period of three weeks is somewhat excessive for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For giving evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And I don't have any problem with that, because I don't think he'll be anywhere near that long. He will certainly be a substantial witness, but I don't think he will be -- my estimate as I stand here is that he would not be anywhere near a period of three weeks. Because of that, I hope and plan to continue proofing him on Monday and Tuesday and Wednesday, when I can get access to him at the prison, and therefore that I would hope to call him later in the week. That wouldn't cause any let-up in business or proceedings for the Chamber because we have witnesses available, including one who is flying in from Bosnia. Even if he were to start later this week, I hope on Thursday, I'm confident that we would finish his testimony in that period of time that you've allocated already, and his actual testimony wouldn't come close to three weeks. So because of that, I hope that the Chamber will be able to give us some leeway and allow us to continue on Monday with this witness, call the next witness, and then get him on after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is wondering whether, from what you have said, your intention is to start Todorovic on Thursday next week. MR. DI FAZIO: To aim for him to start his testimony on Thursday, as a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If not earlier than that. MR. DI FAZIO: If not earlier. If not earlier, possibly late Wednesday. And in the meantime, to finish this witness and another witness. Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Jelena Kapetanovic, who is coming in from Bosnia. I might add that looking at your order, there seem to be two things that were troubling the Chamber. One was the excessive period of time that was being sought for his testimony. I hope I can set your minds at rest on that. My estimate is that he won't be anywhere near three weeks. I just can't see that. I can't speak for the Defence, of course, but as far as the Prosecution is concerned -- obviously he's going to give evidence for a number of days and I haven't finished proofing him, so I can't give you a final or really accurate estimate, but I would think in the order of three to four days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll leave it to the Prosecution, then. MR. DI FAZIO: And another matter, if I may add also to assist you and perhaps set the Chamber's mind at greater ease, is this: Another reason you were concerned about was that there would be a lack of contact between any other people at the Detention Centre. That is now limited, I think you know, as I sought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That was varied. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But the Trial Chamber is not allowing -- does not wish to allow the time taken for proofing as having been allowed by the Trial Chamber. That's the point I want to make. Because as far as the order is concerned, he's supposed to start his testimony on Monday, at 9.00. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Fair enough, we have had this problem with this witness who cannot continue, and we have to finish him, but the Trial Chamber expected that as soon as we finished with the current witness, then we would go on to him. But the Trial Chamber will leave that to the Prosecution, as long as there is no excessive stay of the witness who is in fact supposed to be serving his sentence. MR. DI FAZIO: The way I plan things, I don't expect that his evidence will be taking three weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber will trust the Prosecution with that. Any matter with the Defence? MR. DI FAZIO: I understand my colleague Mr. Weiner has a matter that he wishes to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One last matter. We received another document at the break, at this past break, the one that they started to show the witness and he said he had never -- you know, didn't have a chance to look at it. May I have permission to see the witness - probably not today, probably just before Monday morning - and go through it with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if I could do it in re-direct, I know what the document is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. You can do so. Any matters from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would be very grateful if we could know -- my understanding is next week we are working from 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall start sitting in the morning from 9.00. The session starts at 9.00 sharp, so everybody has to be here before 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Until --?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Until 1345.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 1345. Okay. Another matter: I think that -- well, we have to see from our learned friends from the Prosecution, because you can understand the position of the Defence. We are a little bit confused about the witness schedule, who is going to come, how we can arrange. So I hope next week -- because otherwise, you know, we have three perilous issues now. For example, Variant A is Mrs. Jelena Kapetanovic, Variant B is Stevan Todorovic, Variant C is Mrs. Ewa Tabeau. So we are a little bit -- I mean, we have to be ready immediately, according to my information, for all of these witnesses. But we appreciate your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think the Prosecution have made it clear that after we finish the current witness, it's Kapetanovic and then Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's for next week, so you can prepare for this one and those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And another matter which I want to raise to this Honourable Chamber is of vital importance, I would say, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you might be aware that there is certain, I would say, initiative from the Defence counsel here working within the Tribunal to clarify their position and to see possible improvement of the conditions of the work of the Defence counsel. But for our particular team, I kindly ask - of course, if it's possible; of course, according to the security rules and the other measures - that we, during these short breaks that we have in Courtroom 3, have limited access, escorted access, whenever it's possible, to the terrace. Your Honours, we don't have fresh air. It's really absolutely complicated for the short break to pass all these doors, to come to our Defence room, and then to be back, while, at the same time, all others have the access. And now there is a party going right now. I don't want to party. I just want a little bit of fresh break, you know, fresh air, Your Honours. It's serious. Months and months are here. I mean, if you can help us, please; in not, thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I would have thought that you would have made that application with the Registrar's Office. Because then the Registrar would make arrangements, if possible, to allow the Defence counsel to go outside to the terrace during the breaks, during proceedings. I think you should approach the Office of the Registrar for that, because they're the ones who decide the passages for every party coming to the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, obviously that would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Including the Prosecution. There are certain sections of the building, including the Judges, there are certain sections of this building where we don't have access. So I think it's better to approach the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Everyone has access to the terrace, Your Honours. But my idea is if you could just give a few words to the representative of the Registry in support of our situation, just that. I mean, if not, I mean, I appreciate your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Pantelic. That's understood. We shall adjourn now until Monday. The proceedings will start at 9.00 sharp.
